caption_draft: Overview of the proposed CeNN-based functional-emulation framework. A tuned QELM reference model provides prediction targets and observable-level features, while the CeNN produces forecasting and emulation outputs. The framework is evaluated as a classical functional emulator, not as a quantum-state simulator.
Experimental coverage matrix. The revised benchmark evaluates ten models on six real datasets using the same leakage-safe chronological protocol.
Forecasting benchmark across six real datasets. MASE is used as the primary scale-free forecasting metric; lower values indicate better performance.
article_purpose: forecasting performance across datasets and baselines

caption_draft: Ranking summary based on MASE. This figure identifies dataset-specific strengths without implying universal superiority of any single model.
Functional-emulation fidelity measured by Pearson correlation between CeNN outputs and QELM teacher outputs. Higher values indicate stronger functional alignment.
Forecasting--emulation trade-off. The figure separates direct forecasting accuracy from QELM functional alignment and helps interpret CeNN_NS and CeNN_Emulator as different operating points.
Accuracy--efficiency trade-off. Bubble size is proportional to parameter count, while the axes summarize mean forecasting error and inference latency.

Paired comparison summary. Negative delta means CeNN_NS has lower MASE than the comparator. Statistical p-values and effect sizes are exported in the CSV files; full significance testing requires full mode with multiple seeds.
Forecast diagnostics across the six real datasets. The panel compares the true test sequence with QELM, CeNN_NS, CeNN_Emulator, and the best model by MASE for each dataset.
